Ancient Indian History — 350 Practice Questions with Answers

Ancient Indian history covers the period from prehistory to about the eighth century CE. The questions here range from the Indus Valley Civilisation and the Vedic age to the Mauryas, the Guptas and the rise of Buddhism and Jainism.

Prehistory and the Indus Valley

The Stone Age cultures of India were followed by the Indus Valley Civilisation, a bronze-age urban culture of Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Lothal and Kalibangan. Its town planning, drainage, seals and script are the main exam points.

The Vedic Age and the Mahajanapadas

The Rigvedic and later Vedic periods saw the growth of the varna system, the Sabha and Samiti, and the sixteen Mahajanapadas. Magadha emerged as the strongest kingdom and became the base of the Mauryan empire.

Empires, Religion and Culture

Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan empire and Ashoka spread Buddhism through his edicts. The Gupta age is called the golden age for its art, science and literature. Buddhism and Jainism, founded by the Buddha and Mahavira, reshaped Indian religion.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which period does ancient Indian history cover?

It covers the period from prehistoric times up to about the eighth century CE, ending with the decline of the later Guptas.

Who founded the Mauryan empire?

Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan empire around 322 BCE with the help of Chanakya, also called Kautilya.

Why is the Gupta period called the golden age?

Because of major achievements in art, architecture, mathematics, astronomy and Sanskrit literature, including the works of Kalidasa and the discoveries of Aryabhata.
